structural_finding.summary: The V7 pair-specific Local Factor uses the arithmetic mean of standardized predeclared controls as the one common pair-excluded factor. That basis is not invariant to opposite probability coding of economically related controls and can collapse to zero even when every control is driven perfectly by the same latent factor.

code_contract.control_selection: metadata/text only; no return-orientation or sign-alignment condition is imposed
code_contract.why_material: predeclared controls can include contracts whose YES probabilities load with opposite signs on the same event state; equal-weight averaging then destroys the shared factor before loading, residual, unit-root and hedge inference

structural_finding.interpretation: This is an identification/power defect, not alpha evidence. It can make broader universes anti-monotone: adding strongly related but oppositely coded controls can make a formerly identifiable common factor unestimable or unstable.

required_common_sample_comparison: target-excluded first principal component of the same frozen controls
another pre-specified control-only orientation rule used only as a diagnostic comparator
promotion_gates_after_factor_repair: pair/control graph frozen before target price inference
one common factor basis shared by both targets and invariant up to global sign to opposite control coding
conditional residual unit-root bootstrap that reconstructs level paths under the marginal null
dependence-robust multiplicity over the full predeclared family
